evidence: Charis. 2 and 3; Diom. 1 (Lewis & Short s.v. impersōnālis)
terms.comment: A verb used only in the third person, as pudet, licet, piget. The term is the later grammarians’; Quintilian describes such verbs as those that tertiae dēmum persōnae figūrā dīcuntur, are said only in the form of the third person (1.4.28).

phrases.latin: quaedam tertiae dēmum persōnae figūrā dīcuntur ut licet, piget
phrases.english: some are said only in the form of the third person, as licet, piget

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 225, p. 230, p. 246.
